Subject: Notice — temporary APAC relay proxy and subprocessor roster (planned Nov 10–17)

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Wanted to give early notice that EdgeWave will enable a temporary relay/proxy cluster in APAC (relay.edgewave-apac.net) for load relief on Nov 10–17 while we complete a regional capacity upgrade. During that window a subset of telemetry and observability streams for customers hosted in APAC may transit through our APAC relay. No customer content will be stored beyond 48 hours; we will maintain TLS in transit and limit egress to our relay nodes.

Action we need from Redwood:
- Confirm whether this temporary relay counts as a subprocessor change under our DPA for Acme Payments (we believe it does).
- Provide a reconciliation of processors that will see routed telemetry (K/V stores, monitoring vendors).
- Indicate any onshore fallback or blocking requirements for sensitive accounts (Acme Payments flagged for APAC residency).

I've attached a current EdgeWave subprocessor roster and a network map for the relay (edgewave_subprocessor_roster_20281103.csv, apac_relay_network_map_20281103.pdf). We can provide additional evidence (SOC2 scope, IP ranges) on request.

Tim (Acme): including you so your SRE/infosec team can flag any hard blockers early.

- Jason Park
EdgeWave Operations

Jason / EdgeWave team — thanks for the heads up. A few immediate notes from Redwood: 

1) We treat any new relay or proxy that processes telemetry or tokens as a subprocessor change for affected customers. Please assume this triggers the subprocessor notification workflow for accounts with residency constraints (Acme).

2) We need the following evidence by Nov 6 to route through our internal review process:
   - Confirmation of storage retention policy for relay nodes (you state 48 hrs, need explicit retention TTL for each storage type).
   - Certs/IP/CIDR ranges for the relay endpoints.
   - Clarify whether any logs contain PII or user identifiers (unique client ids, account ids).

3) Action items (Redwood):
   - Kimberly: lead the compliance review and confirm whether this requires a DPA addendum for Acme.
   - Laura: coordinate account contacts at Acme and confirm whether they require an onshore-only fallback.
   - I will prepare a short advisory and temporary routing policy to present to Acme security.

If EdgeWave can confirm the three items above and share a signed statement for the temporary window, we can expedite a streamlined approval for monitoring/telemetry traffic only. For clarity, we are not authorizing content storage or long-term export.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Quick compliance checklist from my side (Kimberly):

- DPA impact: if EdgeWave or any downstream subprocessor will access message text, customer-provided prompts, or identifiers beyond ephemeral telemetry we will need a DPA addendum. Please confirm 'telemetry' fields exactly (e.g., only request/response latency metrics vs full request headers).

- KMS/HSM: will the relay touch any encryption keys or perform crypto ops? If yes, provide KMS provider roster and key scopes.

- Escrow / Onshore fallback: For Acme we must ensure an onshore routing fallback (EU/US) able to absorb traffic within 4 hours if requested. Provide confirmation you can roll back routing and the expected failover time.

- Evidence: SOC2 in-scope carveouts and evidence zip (if any) would be helpful. EdgeWave, please indicate which systems in your roster store logs >24h.

I'll draft an interim subprocessor notification and proposed narrow-scope addendum template once the details arrive.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood
From: ops@edgewave.example.com (EdgeWave Operations)

Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Notice — temporary APAC relay proxy and subprocessor roster (planned Nov 10–17)

Thanks for the quick replies — answers below and attached updated roster and SLA workbook.

- Retention: relay nodes will hold only ephemeral buffers and telemetry logs with TTLs set to 48 hours by default; internal metrics aggregates (no request bodies) are retained up to 7 days for operational health. See apac_relay_network_map_20281103.pdf and edgewave_sla_and_inventory.xlsx for per-system TTLs.

- IPs/CIDRs and certs: included in the Drive link and attached CSV.

- PII/Identifiers: relay buffers do not persist request payloads. We may log truncated identifiers (last 8 chars of request_id) for routing correlation; no full prompt or request body is stored.

- KMS/HSM: We do not perform crypto operations at the relay; TLS termination occurs at the edge and keys are managed in our central KMS (KeyCloud). KMS provider is listed in the roster workbook.

- Failover: we can revert routing to US/EU endpoints within ~3 hours — we have a rollback runbook and a standby capacity agreement. We'll include a signed rollback affirmation in the DocuSign link.

Attachments: edgewave_subprocessor_roster_20281103.csv, apac_relay_network_map_20281103.pdf, edgewave_sla_and_inventory.xlsx

If Redwood is comfortable with the above, please confirm by EOD Nov 6 and we'll publish a temporary subprocessor notice for affected customers (Acme, Harborview, and two pilot tenants).

-Jason Park
EdgeWave Operations
